messages.subject: lavaan Package: Error Message
parts:
Hello All,

I am trying to estimate a growth model using 3 observations per respondent and time-varying covariates. The syntax for the "lavaan" package in R is shown below. 

model <- ' 
  # Intercept and slope with fixed coefficient
  i =~ 1 * LocalBillings_1 + 1 * LocalBillings_2 + 1 * LocalBillings_3
  s =~ 0 * LocalBillings_1 + 1 * LocalBillings_2 + 2 * LocalBillings_3

  # regressions
  i ~ Size1 + Size2
  s ~ Size1 + Size2

  # time-varying covariates
  LocalBillings_1 ~ L11_1
  LocalBillings_2 ~ L11_2
  LocalBillings_3 ~ L11_3
'

However, I get the error message below.

fit <- growth(model,data=TotalRevenue,estimator="ML",control=list(x.tol=1e-6))
Error in lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: initial model-implied matrix (Sigma) is not positive definite;
  check your model and/or starting parameters.

Your feedback would be greatly appreciated.

Ziad Elmously

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: lavaan Package: Error Message
parts:
First, is the model plausible for your data? If the model badly misfits your data, estimation can be challenging.
     Second, the message says that Sigma is n.p.d. to start. If you supply starting values for parameters. The most critical parameters are probably the variances for i and s. If you set these at positive values away from 0,like
i~~start(0.5)*i
s~~start(0.5)*s
     That might help the initial Sigma to be positive definite.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: lavaan Package: Error Message
parts:
If you think that i and s have a negative covariance, try a value closer to 0 like -0.3. If i and s each have variances of 0.5 and their covariance is -0.5, then their correlation is -1, making their correlation matrix n.p.d. That produces the second message.
    I am sorry, I gave you bad advice on the first message.If the sample covariance matrix cannot be inverted, then the same matrix itself is n.p.d. That is not a function of model parameters. You need to examine that covariance matrix yourself--if D is your data set, then
>cov(D)
or
>round(cov(D),3)
to round the estimates to 3 decimal places

You may find that the correlation matrix
>cor(D)
makes it easier to see the problem.
     Sorry for the misdirection.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: lavaan Package: Error Message
parts:
> fit <-
> growth(model,data=TotalRevenue,estimator="ML",control=list(x.tol=1e-6))
> Error in lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats =
> lavsamplestats, :
> lavaan ERROR: initial model-implied matrix (Sigma) is not positive
> definite;
> check your model and/or starting parameters.

Try this:

fit <- growth(model,data=TotalRevenue,estimator="ML", do.fit = FALSE)

This will NOT fit the data. But still process the model, data, etc...
and give you back a lavaan object that can be inspected.

Next, try:

fitted(fit)$cov

and you will *see* the initial model-implied covariance matrix (Sigma).
Look for covariances that are larger than the corresponding variances.

Finally, add better starting values to avoid this (make sure the implied
variances are large enough).

Yves.
